Gate B gains a NON-BLOCKING row: the MPI-458 confirmation run (full test:desktop concurrent with npm start). MPI-458 itself closed as NOT A DEFECT in a5320d67 - the desktop suite does not steal the user's single-instance lock, measured three ways on Electron 41.1.1 - so docs/testing.md needs no waiver, the release notes need no line, and there is nothing to fold. The row exists only so the deferred confirmation is visible instead of forgotten; it was deferred because the live smoke run held the machine, and no source was changed so it cannot regress 1.4. Two decisions inherited onto the umbrella: (1) the proposed CUBRIC_E2E lock exemption was deliberately NOT shipped and must be REJECTED if it returns as hardening - it fixes nothing and would let a spec that forgot CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA boot against the real user profile; (2) a parallel app instance needs BOTH its own profile and its own CUBRIC_PORT - a bare second npm start dies in ~2s, exit 0, silently, which is the lock working correctly and not a bug to chase.

Gate B gains a post-smoke verification session that closes MPI-480 acceptance 3 and MPI-481's live check together - same rig, one throwaway 10 GB volume, ~10 minutes. Recorded because BOTH were proposed as things the running smoke test could absorb for free, and neither can: MPI-481's fix lives in routes/, which is read at server fork, so proving it requires RESTARTING the app that is driving the smoke run, and MPI-480's window needs a Pod deliberately caught cold. Spinning a second app instance is not a workaround - MPI-485 proves an instance that touches the remote engine reaps the other's Pod via the name-based orphan sweep, which is exactly what killed run 3 today. So these are strictly AFTER the matrix finishes. The unchanged hazard is written into the row: cancel with a Pod attached calls remoteUninstallDep and deletes volume partials - delete the Pod first.

Gate A gains MPI-483 and its prerequisite MPI-482, on the umbrella's OWN criterion - 1.4 CLAIMS something that is not true. The wake-up-install bullet at UNRELEASED.md:245 reassures the reader that 'genuine failures - a bad file, a full disk - still report exactly as before', making the disk-full path the trustworthy counterexample the bullet rests on. That path is broken: it subtracts du -sb APPARENT bytes, inflated by aria2 preallocation, and told this run '39.4 GB free' when ~91 GB was. So the fix is either the code or the sentence, and shipping both unchanged is not an option. MPI-482 rides in as the prerequisite (a corrected gate fed by guessed sizes is precisely wrong) and is independently user-visible because modelJob.totalBytes is summed from those same strings on both engines - every 1.4 install bar is denominated by a guess. DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED: MPI-485 (orphan sweep) stays out of the gate list - no 1.4 claim touches it and it needs two instances sharing one RunPod key, which is our situation, not a user's; it is already referenced in Gate B as the reason parallel verification is unsafe. MPI-486 (a partial-install bar looks identical to a downloading one) also stays out - it is renderer-only and therefore parallel-safe with the running smoke test, so it can be worked now instead of gated.

(2) Wan t2v 27GB -> 29GB: both halves HEAD-measured at 14,548,461,3xx bytes against a declared 13.55GB each. Both are MPI-482's defect showing up in user-facing copy. (3) The full-disk example is dropped from the wake-up-install bullet, which settles the fourth soft spot WITHOUT waiting on MPI-483 - the sentence is now true either way, and the phrase goes back if 483 lands. One soft spot CLEARED as never having been a gap: 'Resize Video works on a cloud GPU' is live-verified in MPI-438's validation - Pod vhks7b6fl1x57h, prompt 81b0399f, status success, after ensureUniversalNodesOnVolume took object_info 1822 -> 1863 node types. One soft spot got WORSE: the preview-decoder bullet. The note said 'Klein verified, Wan not'; MPI-420's validation leaves ALL THREE live checks unticked and the card was bulk-closed by 5f27d3cb without them, so the 'looks like your picture' claim is unobserved on every model. The install half is solid. Added to Gate B as one Klein + one Wan generation, with the fallback wording if it cannot be run. Remaining FLAGs are decisions for the fold, not defects: install-screen flicker (never seen fire), MPI-480 acceptance 3 and MPI-481 (both zero Pod contact, both on the Gate B throwaway-Pod row), H3's 4K rung (added on the user's call with no run behind it, and the bullet already hedges it), and the two first-run bullets closed without the look they asked for. Claim audit, size half CORRECTED - MPI-482 landed mid-audit (af829e0f) and inverted its own premise. The hand-typed DEPS size strings were 4.1 percent OVER true, not under: HuggingFace's decimal-GB display copied into a field every consumer parses as 1024-based. All 107 are now regenerated from measured bytes and formatted as GiB, so the tile is the only correct source for a GB figure in the release notes. Three restatements, replacing the two this audit made an hour earlier: LTX Balanced now reads '20GB instead of 22-23.5GB' (the OLD half was the wrong unit, not the new one - fp8 measures 23.49 GiB and mxfp8 22.4 GiB, against the 24-25GB decimal figure the bullet had); Wan t2v goes BACK to 27GB, which was right all along because 13.55GB per half was already GiB; and H3 drops from 53GB to 50GB - its bytes are genuinely 53.1 decimal GB and were HEAD-verified in MPI-452, but the five deps now sum to 49.5 GiB on the tile, and the tile is what the reader checks the sentence against. Those are every GB figure in the notes bar two that are byte counts and safe as written: the 25GB stalled dep (MPI-460) and the ~16GB of stranded weights (MPI-462). Recorded because the lesson generalises past this fold: a size in user-facing copy must be read off DEPS, never off a publisher's page.

Gate B live-preview check PASSES on FLUX.2 Klein, observed 20:25Z - the release-note promise 'looks like your picture, not a colour blob' is true. The two findings this umbrella surfaced were actioned rather than left in a report. MPI-509 carries the real defect (a remote install answering success:true having installed nothing when the engine dep filter empties the request) and is linked here as explicitly NOT gating 1.4 - pre-existing, not a regression, no user path reaches it. The HuggingFace staging finding needed no card: MPI-491 is already done/complete and the finding is a fact rather than owed work, so it went to docs/download-manager.md where the router sends people - an in-flight HF install reads 49,664 bytes on the volume with 1.27GB fetched, then jumps to the full 26.37GB on completion, which also means an HF dep can never exercise partial .part behaviour.

Gate B's throwaway-Pod session is DONE and both cards it carried are closed. MPI-483 measured in one request via GET /remote/pod/ls: phantomBytes never left +/-15MB across a 14.31GB aria2 install, so a RunPod network volume allocates the full declared length immediately and du -sb == du -s --block-size=1 - bug 1's sparse-.part premise is disproven and the shipped flag swap is a correctness tidy, NOT a 48.65GB fix; that gap is explained by the two figures being sampled minutes apart during an active fill. Bug 2's free-space gate is unaffected and stays. Consequence recorded on the checklist: the full-disk phrase stays OUT of the wake-up-install bullet permanently, not pending a check. MPI-481 proven live twice - a Pod STOP (not a delete) leaves the app holding a downloading record, and the reinstall logged 'stale in-flight record ... reinstalling' + 'Requeued' on both the HuggingFace and aria2/R2 paths. Gate A now has no open card. Two doc corrections in docs/download-manager.md: the HF path stages INSIDE MODELS_DIR (.part.hfstage), reversing yesterday's note which was built on /remote/pod/disk's 60s du cache; and a killed install strands that staging tree with nothing to sweep it, while the disk gate counts a dep's own stranded .part against its retry.
